title: Name and favorite flower across a session boundary
measures: Baseline identity recall: whether the system retains two stated personal facts (a name and a preference) across 50 intervening turns and a new session. This is a floor, not a ceiling. Passing it shows storage and retrieval work; it says nothing yet about continuity. Systems that fail here will usually fail most other tests.

character.name: Wren
character.description: A warm, curious florist who runs a small shop and chats with regular customers.
character.speech_style: Friendly, conversational, occasionally uses plant metaphors.

setup.event: User says her favorite flower is lavender because it reminds her of her grandmother's garden.

history.content: Hi! I'm Sarah. I just moved to the neighborhood.
Welcome, Sarah! Always nice to meet a new neighbor. Are you a flower person, or just browsing?
Definitely a flower person. My favorite is lavender. It reminds me of my grandmother's garden.
Lavender is a lovely choice, and a grandmother's garden is the best reason to love a flower.

delay.note: Filler is split across sessions 1 and 2 (see results/methodology.md, 'Assembling a test').

probe.prompt: Quick quiz before I buy anything: do you remember my name and my favorite flower?

behavior: may mention the grandmother's garden, but does not need to
must_not: claims never to have met the user

rubric.0: Claims not to know the user, or invents a different name and flower with confidence.
rubric.1: Gets neither fact right but hedges, or asks the user to repeat both.
rubric.2: Gets one fact right and the other wrong.
rubric.3: Gets one fact right and openly says it does not remember the other.
rubric.4: Gets both facts right, but awkwardly (e.g. recites them like a database lookup, breaking character).
rubric.5: Gets both facts right, naturally and in character; may connect lavender to the grandmother's garden.

automatic_checks.description: Response must use the name Sarah.

rationale: Both facts are stated plainly and never contradicted. Because the probe is in a new session, a system that relies only on its context window will fail.
